function.description: Find local movie theatres and their schedule for a specific movie Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. San Diego, CA

The function expects location: string, movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], time: string[]. So we need to call the function twice? The user wants two theaters. We can call the function twice with different locations? Or we can call once with location "San Diego, CA" and movie array containing both movies? But the function signature: movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[] means movie can be either "Tenet" or "No Time To Die" or an array of those? The type is ambiguous. It says movie: "Tenet" | "No Time To Die"[], so movie can be a string "Tenet" or an array of "No Time To Die"? That seems wrong. Probably they want movie: ("Tenet" | "No Time To Die")[] meaning an array of either. But the type is incorrectly defined. We'll assume we can pass an array of movies. So we can call find_movie_showing with location "San Diego, CA", movie ["Tenet", "No Time To Die"], time ["17:00", "19:30"]. That should return theaters that have both showtimes. But the user wants two theaters. We might need to call twice with different locations like "San Diego, CA" and "Chula Vista, CA" or "Carlsbad, CA". But the function only returns theaters for a given location. We can call it twice with different locations. But the user didn't specify which locations. They just said "near San Diego". So we can choose two nearby cities: "Chula Vista, CA" and "Carlsbad, CA". Let's do that.

We need to call the function twice: first for Chula Vista, second for Carlsbad. Provide movie array ["Tenet", "No Time To Die"] and times ["17:00", "19:30"]. Then we will output the results.
